name: CA-35
label: Safe D

key_factors: Cargile has raised under $10,000 with only $448 on hand, against Torres's $245,000 war chest
The district leans Democratic by six points and Torres is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Torres near 97% to win
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: Torres pairs a six-point Democratic district lean with a lopsided fundraising advantage over a challenger who has almost no money, and markets price her near certain to win; with no polling available, the forecast rests on those fundamentals.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Torres or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Norma Torres enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by six points. She has raised more than $920,000 and holds roughly $245,000 in cash, while Republican Mike Cargile has raised under $10,000 and reports only a few hundred dollars on hand, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the spending gap.

Prediction markets put Torres's chances near 97 percent, consistent with a comfortable double-digit expected margin. The main uncertainties are the absence of polling in this district and the chance that a shifting national environment compresses margins in otherwise safe seats. Even so, nothing in the fundraising record or district composition points to a competitive contest.
